title: AuthorWhyResult
description:
`author.why` result: the actionable explanation of a staged atom's standing —
the blocking rulings and defeater (why certain / why dead / why possible),
plus the support antichain when the atom is known.

active_supporting_decision_paths.description:
Currently admissible minimal support monomials, with exact recorded
decision names and path boundaries preserved. An empty list means no
support paths are currently admissible; it does not establish standing.

blocked_supports.description:
Minimal symbolic support paths that would be active but for the listed
current direct defeats. This remains separate from active provenance so
a defeated redundant alternative never contaminates a live path.

blocking_defeats.description:
The active direct decision defeats that explain a currently blocked
conclusion. Live conclusions report an explicit empty list; their
blocked alternatives remain available through [`Self::blocked_supports`].

supporting_decisions.description:
The recorded decisions in the atom's support antichain — the support
monomials' claim ids filtered to the known-decision set (contract 1.9.0,
DL-0083). The auditability affordance: it lets a caller confirm a fact
reached certainty through recorded decisions. The field is omitted when
there are no supporting decisions.

why.description: The positive support antichain, present when the world derives the atom.

why_not.description:
The negative explanation: what stands between the atom and certainty (the
closest support, the unruled variables blocking it, the defeater).

BlockedSupport.description: One otherwise-admissible minimal derivation path and its active blockers.

blocking_defeats.description: The minimal active direct-defeat pairs disabling this path.

supporting_decision_path.description: Exact recorded decision ids carried by the fact/rule support monomial.

BlockingDefeat.description: One currently active direct decision attack, named exactly as recorded.

defeated_decision.description: The decision whose supporting path is disabled.

defeating_decision.description: The undefeated decision that directly attacks it.

Status.description: A claim's three-valued standing under `(ν, Θ)`, derived — never stored.

oneOf.description:
Every monomial is `Θ`-unsatisfiable: the claim holds in no admissible
world. (Whether this is rejection or mere supersession is a `C`
question, outside the algebra.)

Some monomial is `Θ`-satisfiable but none is resolved-and-undefeated: the
shadow layer.

Some monomial holds on resolved events alone, with that monomial's own
defeater not fully ruled: assertable.

Why.description:
The positive explanation of an atom: its support antichain rendered for a
reader.

The [`antichain`](Why::antichain) is the disjunction of minimal witnesses —
the same shape as [`crate::SupportIndex::why`], one inner vector of
[`ClaimId`]s per minimal monomial of the support (sign is dropped, matching
that seam). [`rendered`](Why::rendered) is the parallel human line for each
witness, resolved to claim names through the world's interner; a negative
literal renders with a `not ` prefix, and the unconditional witness (the
empty monomial) renders as `unconditional`.

antichain.description: The disjunction of minimal witnesses, each a conjunction of claim ids.

rendered.description: The per-witness human rendering, index-aligned with `antichain`.

WhyNot.description:
The negative explanation of an atom that is not certain: what stands between
it and assertability.

Produced by [`why_not`]. When the atom is unknown (no derivation for it),
[`known`](WhyNot::known) is false and the analysis fields are empty.

atom.description: The atom under scrutiny, rendered `pred(a, b)`.

blocking.description:
The unruled (open) variables of that closest witness: the rulings that,
once made, would carry the claim. Empty when nothing open blocks it (the
obstacle is then a defeater, or the atom is dead).

closest.description:
The live support monomial closest to certainty — the fewest unruled
variables — as claim ids. Empty when the atom is unknown or every
monomial is dead.

defeater.description:
The defeater claim, if the atom rests on a defeasible default a ruling
has overridden or could override — blame.

known.description:
Whether the world derives this atom at all. False means unknown — absent
from certain ∪ possible (`02-semantics.md` §4).

rendered.description:
The human rendering: the blocking rulings and the defeater, resolved to
claim names.

status.description:
The atom's standing under the world's ambient valuation. `Dead` when
unknown.
